caller_is_owner.meaning: the caller of increaseLiquidityCurrentRange() is the owner (onlyOwner satisfied)

pending_tx_observable.meaning: a pending increaseLiquidityCurrentRange() call is observable in the mempool by an MEV bot
pending_tx_observable.checkpoint: before the pending transaction is mined

hold_duration_seconds.meaning: duration the MEV bot holds the pending transaction before it executes (report cites 1 hour, 1 day, 1 week, 1 month)

transaction_executed_after_hold.meaning: the held increaseLiquidityCurrentRange() transaction still executes after being held for hold_duration_seconds
transaction_executed_after_hold.checkpoint: at execution of the held transaction

assumptions: The owner is the caller of increaseLiquidityCurrentRange(); the MEV bot observes the pending owner transaction in the mempool rather than being the owner.
The report's example deadline is block.timestamp + 5 minutes (300 seconds), used as the expiry bound the transaction should respect.

unresolved.description: Report does not state whether the owner is the MEV bot or a separate victim; onlyOwner restricts the caller, so the mempool-hold scenario presumes the attacker is not the owner.
Report gives hold durations only as illustrative ranges (1 hour, 1 day, 1 week, 1 month) without a single concrete bound; the 5-minute deadline is an example, not a stated enforced value.

limitations: Formalizes only impact_indefinite_hold; stale-pricing execution and value extraction are separate impacts handled in other passes.
The 300-second bound is the report's illustrative deadline example; runtime binding of the actual deadline parameter is deferred to code binding.
